passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
The choirmaster leads music in worship.
This psalm is for worship.

passages.text: The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of His hands.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm for the choirmaster.
The heavens show the glory of God.
The skies tell about what God has made.
The skies proclaim the work of God's hands.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם מְֽסַפְּרִ֥ים כְּבֽוֹד־ אֵ֑ל וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דָ֗יו מַגִּ֥יד הָרָקִֽיעַ׃

passages.text: Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge.
passages.sermon:
The heavens and the skies show God's glory.
They show the work of God's hands.
Every day, the heavens speak.
Each day, they pour out speech.
Every night, the skies reveal knowledge.
Each night, they show understanding.
passages.original: י֣וֹם לְ֭יוֹם יַבִּ֣יעַֽ אֹ֑מֶר וְלַ֥יְלָה לְּ֝לַ֗יְלָה יְחַוֶּה־ דָּֽעַת׃

passages.text: Without speech or language, without a sound to be heard, their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In the heavens He has pitched a tent for the sun.
passages.sermon:
The heavens and the skies show God's glory.
They do not use speech.
They do not use words.
No sound comes from them.
But their voice goes out through all the earth.
Their words reach to the ends of the world.
God made a home for the sun in the heavens.
passages.original: אֵֽין־ אֹ֭מֶר וְאֵ֣ין דְּבָרִ֑ים בְּ֝לִ֗י נִשְׁמָ֥ע קוֹלָֽם׃ בְּכָל־ הָאָ֨רֶץ׀ יָ֘צָ֤א קַוָּ֗ם וּבִקְצֵ֣ה תֵ֭בֵל מִלֵּיהֶ֑ם לַ֝שֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ שָֽׂם־ אֹ֥הֶל בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Like a bridegroom emerging from his chamber, like a champion rejoicing to run his course, it rises at one end of the heavens and runs its circuit to the other; nothing is deprived of its warmth.
passages.sermon:
The sun rises in the sky.
God made a place for the sun in the heavens.
The sun comes out like a bridegroom leaving his room.
The sun is joyful like a strong man ready to run a race.
The sun starts at one end of the heavens.
The sun moves across the sky to the other end.
Nothing can hide from the sun’s heat.
Everything on earth feels the sun’s warmth.
passages.original: וְה֗וּא כְּ֭חָתָן יֹצֵ֣א מֵחֻפָּת֑וֹ יָשִׂ֥ישׂ כְּ֝גִבּ֗וֹר לָר֥וּץ אֹֽרַח׃ מִקְצֵ֤ה הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם׀ מֽוֹצָא֗וֹ וּתְקוּפָת֥וֹ עַל־ קְצוֹתָ֑ם וְאֵ֥ין נִ֝סְתָּ֗ר מֵֽחַמָּתוֹ׃

passages.text: The Law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul; the testimony of the LORD is trustworthy, making wise the simple.
passages.sermon:
The Law of the LORD is perfect.
The Law of the LORD restores the soul.
The testimony of the LORD is trustworthy.
The testimony of the LORD makes simple people wise.
passages.original: תּ֘וֹרַ֤ת יְהוָ֣ה תְּ֭מִימָה מְשִׁ֣יבַת נָ֑פֶשׁ עֵד֥וּת יְהוָ֥ה נֶ֝אֱמָנָ֗ה מַחְכִּ֥ימַת פֶּֽתִי׃

passages.text: The precepts of the LORD are right, bringing joy to the heart; the commandments of the LORD are radiant, giving light to the eyes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gives precepts.
These precepts are right.
These precepts bring joy to the heart.
The LORD gives commandments.
These commandments are pure.
These commandments give light to the eyes.
passages.original: פִּקּ֘וּדֵ֤י יְהוָ֣ה יְ֭שָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי־ לֵ֑ב מִצְוַ֥ת יְהוָ֥ה בָּ֝רָ֗ה מְאִירַ֥ת עֵינָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever; the judgments of the LORD are true, being altogether righteous.
passages.sermon:
The fear of the LORD is pure.
It lasts forever.
The judgments of the LORD are true.
They are completely righteous.
passages.original: יִרְאַ֤ת יְהוָ֨ה׀ טְהוֹרָה֮ עוֹמֶ֪דֶת לָ֫עַ֥ד מִֽשְׁפְּטֵי־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱמֶ֑ת צָֽדְק֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃

passages.text: They are more precious than gold, than much pure gold; they are sweeter than honey, than honey from the comb.
passages.sermon:
God’s precepts are very valuable.
They are more precious than gold.
They are more precious than much pure gold.
God’s precepts are very pleasant.
They are sweeter than honey.
They are sweeter than honey from the honeycomb.
passages.original: הַֽנֶּחֱמָדִ֗ים מִ֭זָּהָב וּמִפַּ֣ז רָ֑ב וּמְתוּקִ֥ים מִ֝דְּבַ֗שׁ וְנֹ֣פֶת צוּפִֽים׃

passages.text: By them indeed Your servant is warned; in keeping them is great reward.
passages.sermon:
God gives His laws and judgments.
\r\nGod’s servant learns from them.
\r\nGod’s servant receives warning through them.
\r\nIf a person keeps God’s laws, he receives a great reward.
passages.original: גַּֽם־ עַ֭בְדְּךָ נִזְהָ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְרָ֗ם עֵ֣קֶב רָֽב׃

passages.text: Who can discern his own errors? Cleanse me from my hidden faults.
passages.sermon: A person cannot always see his own errors.\r\nHidden faults are difficult to recognize.\r\nGod, please cleanse me from my hidden faults.

passages.text: Keep Your servant also from willful sins; may they not rule over me. Then I will be blameless and cleansed of great transgression.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David is God's servant.
David asks God to keep him from willful sins.
Willful sins are sins people commit on purpose.
David asks God not to let willful sins rule over him.
David wants to be free from the power of willful sins.
If God keeps him from willful sins, David will be blameless.
If God keeps him from willful sins, David will be cleansed from great transgression.
passages.original: גַּ֤ם מִזֵּדִ֨ים׀ חֲשֹׂ֬ךְ עַבְדֶּ֗ךָ אַֽל־ יִמְשְׁלוּ־ בִ֣י אָ֣ז אֵיתָ֑ם וְ֝נִקֵּ֗יתִי מִפֶּ֥שַֽׁע רָֽב׃

passages.text: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing in Your sight, O LORD, my Rock and my Redeemer.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to the LORD.
David calls the LORD his Rock.
David calls the LORD his Redeemer.
David asks the LORD to accept his words.
David wants his words to please the LORD.
David also asks the LORD to accept his thoughts.
David wants his thoughts to please the LORD.
David wants both his words and his thoughts to be right before the LORD.
passages.original: יִֽהְי֥וּ לְרָצ֨וֹן׀ אִמְרֵי־ פִ֡י וְהֶגְי֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ יְ֝הוָ֗ה צוּרִ֥י וְגֹאֲלִֽי׃
